plan.topic: Pain under the right ribs after a rich meal on tirzepatide: the gallbladder signs on the label, and why rapid weight loss is linked to gallstones
plan.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide and Your Gallbladder: 4 Signs to Know #shorts'. Sentence 1: tirzepatide plus the label's gallbladder trial rates vs placebo, with the population on the card. Then the hedged rapid-weight-loss link, the exact Medication Guide sign list ending 'call your healthcare provider right away', the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', and the loop line.
plan.why: Spin-off of L1: a felt symptom people search, pointing viewers to the Serious Risks video. The last gallbladder Short was 10-26, outside the 30-day window. | fact-check: The topic is sound and it's a real spin-off. The problem is the working title 'Normal?'. It implies pain under the right ribs may be normal, but that is a label warning sign that needs a call to the prescriber. Reframe as signs to know. Use the label's per-arm acute gallbladder rates vs placebo exactly as L1 verified them (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis given separately, each with its placebo figure). Name the trial population and say 'reported in trials', not 'risk is'. Say 'uncommon' only if L1's verified numbers support it. Keep the rapid-weight-loss line hedged and method-neutral ('rapid weight loss, by any method, is linked to gallstones'). Don't say the drug causes gallstones. Copy the Medication Guide wording exactly: 'pain in your upper stomach (abdomen), fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), or clay-colored stools', then 'call your healthcare provider right away'. Don't add 'right ribs' to the quoted card. It can appear only as untagged narration context. Use no anatomy gore or scare visuals. Watch-next: L1 isn't live yet, so target Side Effects.

The Medication Guide says symptoms may include pain in your upper stomach, yellowing of skin or eyes, fever, and clay-colored stools. If you get any of them, tell your healthcare provider right away. Don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
The numbers check out against the Zepbound label, but two things need fixing before this ships.

**What checks out:**
- **s1 and s3:** DailyMed (setid 487cd7e7…, updated 16 Nov 2026) gives the rates for pooled Studies 1 and 2. Gallstones (cholelithiasis) were 1.1% on Zepbound vs 1% on placebo. Gallbladder inflammation (cholecystitis) was 0.7% vs 0.2%.
- **s4:** the NIDDK page lists fast weight loss as a gallstone risk factor. It was last reviewed November 2017.
- **s5 and s6:** the Medication Guide says "Tell your healthcare provider right away" and uses the "may include" hedge.
- **Word count:** I recounted 106 spoken words, which is inside the 90–120 tight arm.
- **Safety:** the closing lines are correct and nothing in the script is unsafe.

**What needs fixing:**
1. **s5 sign order (minor):** the script says it follows the guide's order, but it doesn't. The Medication Guide lists the signs as upper stomach pain, fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), then clay-colored stools. I checked this twice. The script has fever and yellowing swapped.
2. **S2 revised date (the ship-blocker):** I found the date. The Medication Guide on DailyMed reads "Revised: 11/2026". The source title needs that date, and the source should point to a URL I could actually read. Once this is applied, the hold can be lifted.

issues.claim: "The Medication Guide says symptoms may include pain in your upper stomach, yellowing of skin or eyes, fever, and clay-colored stools." The notes say this is in the guide's order.
issues.problem: The Zepbound Medication Guide (Revised 11/2026) lists the signs in a different order: pain in your upper stomach (abdomen), fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), clay-colored stools. The script and list card put yellowing before fever, so the claim that it follows the guide's order is false.
issues.fix: Narration: "The Medication Guide says symptoms may include pain in your upper stomach, fever, yellowing of skin or eyes, and clay-colored stools." List card items, in this order: "Pain in your upper stomach (abdomen)" / "Fever" / "Yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice)" / "Clay-colored stools". The word count stays at 21.
